assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology and incretin-based therapy is a rare complete arc from hormone biology to drugs that have changed the treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with large outcome trials showing cardiovascular and renal benefit. Originality, clarity and lasting impact are all high. Although my own field is neuroscience, the central appetite-regulating action and the scale of clinical effect make this the strongest case on the list.
assessment.attribution: Holst characterised the physiology and secretion of GLP-1, Drucker established its biology, intestinotrophic and glucoregulatory actions and the therapeutic rationale, and Mojsov identified the bioactive truncated peptide GLP-1(7-36). Lotte Bjerre Knudsen (industrial drug development of liraglutide and semaglutide) is the obvious fourth name, so the three-person limit forces a choice; I would favour the three discovery-side scientists. The priority question around Mojsov versus other laboratories needs careful review.
assessment.maturity: Mature and well confirmed: first approvals date back to 2005 and use has expanded widely since, with independent replication across many trials. Recognition is timely and, if anything, pressing given public prominence.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit among the many contributors (including Habener-type early work and drug-development scientists) is contested and cannot be fully resolved from the supplied names.
The three-laureate cap excludes Knudsen, whose contribution is substantial.
I am relying on my own recollection of the history rather than independent verification.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics provided a general tool to control genetically defined cells with light, transforming causal dissection of neural circuits and spreading to cardiac, retinal and other physiology. Methodological invention of exceptional breadth, originality and impact, and relevant to circuit-level understanding of Parkinson's disease, depression and other disorders in the clinical areas I know.
assessment.attribution: A credible configuration is the discovery of channelrhodopsin function (Nagel, Hegemann, with Bamberg as co-discoverer) plus its adaptation as a neuronal tool (Deisseroth, Boyden, with Miesenböck's earlier genetically targeted photostimulation). The six credited names exceed the three-person limit, so excluding Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenböck is a real injustice risk. I choose Nagel, Hegemann and Deisseroth as the most commonly cited trio.
assessment.maturity: Mature: the core work is from 2002 to 2005 and has been confirmed in thousands of independent laboratories. Initial therapeutic translation (retinal optogenetics for vision restoration) is early, but the tool value is long established. Timely.
uncertainties: Attribution is the principal obstacle: six strong claimants and a three-person limit.
Priority between Miesenböck's and Boyden/Deisseroth's neuronal demonstrations is disputed in the literature.
Whether the prize category fits a research tool rather than a disease discovery is a judgement call, though there is precedent.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new intracellular signalling logic in which the endoplasmic reticulum reports its folding state to the nucleus, via Ire1 splicing of HAC1/XBP1 mRNA and the downstream transcriptional programme. It is a conceptually clean and original discovery with broad relevance to secretory-cell physiology, diabetes, cancer and neurodegeneration, including the proteostasis themes familiar from Parkinson's disease.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori are the clearly decisive figures: Mori identified the transcriptional response and the HAC1 pathway, and Walter identified Ire1 and the unconventional splicing mechanism. The pair is a natural and clean configuration, with only a modest question of whether a third name (e.g., from the earlier ER-stress observations, such as Kozutsumi or Kaufman) is being omitted from the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely confirmed over three decades, with a stable interpretation and conserved mechanism. Direct therapeutic validation is still developing (e.g., integrated stress response modulators), so the clinical dimension is less complete than for other candidates, but the basic science is well established. Timely.
uncertainties: Earlier contributors to the ER-stress response may have claims not captured in the supplied credit.
Clinical translation is incomplete.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TNF blockade established that targeting a single cytokine can control chronic inflammatory disease, opening the biologic era for rheumatoid arthritis, Crohn's disease, psoriasis and other conditions. The discovery was both a conceptual proof (TNF as a master regulator in the cytokine network) and a major clinical advance with lasting global impact.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini are the central pair for the translational concept, from demonstrating TNF's dominant role in rheumatoid synovium to the first clinical trials of anti-TNF. The pair is clean and well recognised. Contributions from the cytokine biology of TNF itself (e.g., Cerami, Beutler, Old) are outside the supplied credit and might be raised by others.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: clinical use since the late 1990s, confirmed by many randomized trials and biosimilars. Recognition is arguably overdue rather than premature, which is a minor concern for urgency but not for merit.
uncertainties: Debate about how to treat the underlying TNF discovery (Old, Cerami, Beutler) versus the clinical translation.
Antibody engineering and development partners are not credited here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway revealed how cytosolic DNA is sensed and converted by a second messenger (cGAMP) into interferon and inflammatory responses. It links antiviral defence, autoimmunity (e.g., interferonopathies) and tumour immunity, and is conceptually original with strong mechanistic clarity.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and the second messenger cGAMP, which is the decisive mechanistic step; Barber identified STING and its role in DNA-driven interferon induction. Ishikawa (co-discoverer of STING), Sun and Wu (Chen laboratory) are also credited, so the allocation is not fully clean. Chen and Barber is the most defensible pair.
assessment.maturity: Fairly mature mechanistically, with independent structural and genetic confirmation, but therapeutic translation (STING agonists and inhibitors) has not yet produced a clear approved benefit, so clinical impact remains prospective. Recognition is plausible but arguably slightly early.
uncertainties: Therapeutic validation is still lacking.
Ishikawa's claim over STING identification versus Barber's is not resolvable from the supplied information.
Credit within the Chen group (Sun, Wu) is ambiguous.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered CAR-T cells produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell leukaemia and lymphoma, which is a clear and dramatic clinical breakthrough with a new therapeutic modality (living drugs) and a growing set of approved products.
assessment.attribution: June (the CD19 CAR trials in CLL and ALL, with costimulatory domain design), Sadelain (CD28-based second-generation CARs and preclinical design) and Rosenberg (TIL therapy and early gene-modified lymphocyte work) represent a plausible trio. The originators of the CAR concept (Eshhar) and the costimulatory CAR work of others are outside the supplied credit, so the attribution picture is incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Mature in B-cell malignancies, with independent trials and regulatory approvals since 2017. Longer-term durability, toxicity and the failure so far in solid tumours leave the picture incomplete, and the field is still moving, which argues for some patience.
uncertainties: Eshhar's foundational CAR concept is not in the credited names.
Whether Rosenberg's inclusion is appropriate for CAR specifically versus adoptive cell therapy more broadly is arguable.
Limited efficacy in solid tumours and safety issues.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of orexin/hypocretin and its loss in narcolepsy type 1 explained a sleep disorder through a defined neuropeptide system, linking neurochemistry to behaviour and disease. As a neurologist I regard this as a model of circuit-level disease understanding, with a first-in-class orexin receptor antagonist now in clinical use for insomnia.
assessment.attribution: Sakurai and Yanagisawa discovered orexin and its receptors and the narcolepsy phenotype in knockout mice; Mignot identified the canine narcolepsy gene (Hcrtr2) and the human loss of orexin neurons; de Lecea and Kilduff independently described hypocretin. Five names are credited, so a three-person configuration necessarily excludes de Lecea and Kilduff, creating a priority issue. Yanagisawa, Sakurai and Mignot is the strongest triad in my view.
assessment.maturity: Mature: findings from 1998 to 2000 replicated widely, and pharmacological translation (suvorexant and related drugs; agonists in development for narcolepsy) supports the mechanism. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Independent near-simultaneous discovery by de Lecea and Kilduff complicates priority.
The magnitude of clinical impact is smaller than that of the broad therapeutic candidates above.
Orexin agonist therapy for narcolepsy is still under development.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib and BCR-ABL inhibition transformed chronic myeloid leukaemia from a fatal disease into a manageable chronic condition and established the paradigm of molecularly targeted cancer therapy. The impact on both patient survival and drug-development strategy is exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (chemistry and kinase inhibitor programme at Ciba-Geigy), Druker (clinical translation and trials) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors) are the natural trio and match prior major prize recognition. Upstream work on BCR-ABL itself (Rowley, Witte, Baltimore and others) is outside the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with two decades of survival data and independent confirmation. Recognition is arguably late rather than premature; a risk is that the field has long been seen as honoured by other awards, but this is not a scientific objection.
uncertainties: The role of earlier BCR-ABL discovery scientists (Rowley, Witte, Baltimore) is not captured.
Whether Sawyers or the industry chemists (e.g., Zimmermann) should be included is debatable.
